title: fix(plugin-calendar): a week or day view move keeps the event's own length and grab point (objectui#11037)
body:
Fixes #11037

Clause-②: no

## What this changes

`packages/plugin-calendar/src/CalendarView.tsx`, the week and day views' time grid (`TimeGridView`). A move now carries the EVENT, not the piece that was grabbed.

- The grid draws an event that crosses midnight as one piece per day, clipped at midnight, and a short event as a piece at least 15 minutes tall. The move used to take its length (`durationMin`) and its grab offset (`grabMinuteOffset`) from that piece, and held the moved piece inside the drop day.
- The move's drag state now carries `durationMs`, the event's own `end - start`, and `grabOffsetMs`, the grabbed point's distance from the event's own start. Both are elapsed time between instants, read from the event (`timedEventInstants`, the same start/end the piece model already derived, including the one-hour default for an event with no end).
- The new start is the drop row minus the grab offset, snapped to `slotMinutes` as before (`movedStartMinutes`), placed on the grid's clock with `setHours` as before. The new end is that start plus `durationMs`.
- An event drawn wholly inside one day (its piece is both its start and its end) is still held inside the drop day, exactly as before. An event that crosses midnight is placed where it is dropped, so its start may land on the day before the drop day, or it may stay overnight.
- The drag preview uses the same computation: it is labelled with the whole event's times and drawn over the part of the event that falls on the drop day.

No change to the month grid, to `ObjectCalendar`'s drop handler, to the resize handles, or to any stored-value shape.

## Measured before, on `origin/main` `30f912a0d`

The new pin file run against the unmodified `CalendarView.tsx` (suite zone UTC, then the forks child):

- A 22:00 to 02:00 event (Jan 12 to Jan 13) dragged by its first piece to Jan 14 10:00: `onEventDrop` got `10:00 to 12:00`, 120 minutes. The card's case, reproduced.
- The same event grabbed at the top of its second piece (its own 00:00, Jan 13) and dropped at Jan 14 10:00: `onEventDrop` got `10:00 to 12:00`, 120 minutes, the start put where the event's midnight had been grabbed.
- Grabbed by its second piece at 01:00 and dropped at Jan 15 01:00: `00:00 to 02:00` on Jan 15.
- Grabbed by its first piece and dropped at 23:00: `22:00 to 00:00`, held inside the drop day.
- A 10:00 to 10:05 event moved: written 15 minutes long, the drawn piece's height.

## The brief's arithmetic, corrected

The dispatch brief said that grabbing the second piece at 00:00 and dropping at 10:00 must land the event at "20:00 to 00:00 the day before the drop's day". That is not what keeping the grab point under the pointer gives: the grabbed point is 2 hours into the event (22:00 to 00:00), so the start lands 2 hours before the drop row. The event is written 08:00 to 12:00 on the drop day, and the grid shows it there as one piece. That is what the pin holds.

## DST

Elapsed length keeps a `datetime` event's real duration, under objectui#10866's reading that a `datetime` keeps its instant. On the night a DST change falls in, the wall clock shows the length an hour longer or shorter. Measured under `America/Los_Angeles`: a 22:00 to 02:00 PDT event (Oct 27 to Oct 28, 2026) moved by its first piece onto Oct 31 22:00 is written `2026-11-01T05:00Z` to `2026-11-01T09:00Z`: 22:00 PDT to 01:00 PST, still 4 elapsed hours. The clock reads 22:00 to 01:00. The same move onto an ordinary night (Oct 29) reads 22:00 to 02:00, and under `Asia/Shanghai` (no DST) onto Oct 31 it reads 22:00 to 02:00.

## Pins

`packages/plugin-calendar/src/__tests__/CalendarView.timeGridMoveDuration-11037.test.tsx`, registered in the forks driver `scripts/__tests__/date-only-zone-pins-10183.test.ts` (its `PINS` list), because a zone written inside the normal run does not move (the root config runs `pool: 'threads'` and pins `UTC`).

Suite zone (runs in the normal run too):
- first piece dropped at 10:00 keeps 4 hours (`10:00 to 14:00`);
- second piece grabbed at its own 00:00, dropped at 10:00: `08:00 to 12:00`, the grabbed point under the pointer;
- second piece grabbed at 01:00, dropped at 01:00 two days on: the same night two days later (`22:00 to 02:00`);
- first piece dropped at 23:00 stays overnight (`23:00 to 03:00`);
- the day view, where only the second piece is on screen: grabbed at 00:00, dropped at 03:00, written `01:00 to 05:00`;
- a 5-minute event keeps 5 minutes;
- while dragging, the preview reads `10:00 AM – 2:00 PM`;
- controls, green before and after: a same-day event moves as before (1 hour kept); a same-day event dropped at 23:30 is still held inside the drop day (`22:00 to 00:00`); an event with no end is still handed an end one hour after its new start.

Driven: `America/Los_Angeles` (rig, fixture validity, the fall-back case, the ordinary-night twin) and `Asia/Shanghai` (rig, the no-DST control).

**Red leg**, from the committed fix: `CalendarView.tsx` put back to the base's bytes and the pin file run in the forks child: `Tests 10 failed | 6 passed (16)`. The 6 that pass are the three controls, the two rigs and the fixture-validity case. Restored with `git checkout HEAD`, proved by the file's blob hash equal to the HEAD blob and an empty `git diff HEAD`. **Green leg** at `5ce5efca2`: `Tests 16 passed (16)`.

## Gates, at `5ce5efca2`

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-calendar/`: `Test Files 56 passed (56)`, `Tests 375 passed | 91 skipped (466)` (the skipped are the package's driven zone cases).
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-calendar type-check` (both `tsc --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0. `--listFiles` of the test project includes the new pin file. Dependency closure built first (`turbo run build --filter=@object-ui/plugin-calendar^...`).
- eslint, narrowed to the touched files (the repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's): the population is the `**/*.{ts,tsx}` files `eslint.config.js` lints, of which this diff touches three (the changeset is markdown); `--format json` reported 3 files, 0 errors. `CalendarView.tsx` carries 24 warnings, the same count per rule as the base's bytes linted under the same path. The narrowing excludes nothing: `eslint.config.js` sets no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService` (no type-aware rule) and no rule under `eslint-rules/` reads another file, so this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file.
- `scripts/__tests__`: the zone-pin driver, `spawned-vitest-child-env-8616`, the changeset gate tests (claims, fixed, no-major, overwrite, presence, pending literals, polarity census), `check-control-bytes` and `check-new-cross-file-line-citations`: `Test Files 11 passed (11)`, `Tests 400 passed (400)`.
- `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-overwrite`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-claims`, `check-pending-changeset-literals`, `check-control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check-test-path-roots`, `check-vi-mock-specifiers`: all exit 0.
- `check-governed-queue-guard --test` over the four changed paths: NOT GOVERNED.
- No import added; the console's eager graph is not touched.

## Acceptance notes

- The drag preview changed with the move: it now shows the whole event's times, and for an event that crosses midnight it draws only the part on the drop day. It keeps a 15-minute minimum height, as a piece has.
- The same-day hold (an event inside one day stays inside the drop day) is unchanged. It is kept on purpose so a same-day event cannot be turned into an overnight one by a drop near the bottom of a column.
- An event with no end is still handed an end one hour after its new start, as before.
- An event whose stored end is earlier than its start now keeps that negative length on a move; before, it came back 15 minutes long. No producer of such an event was looked for.
- All-day and date-only events are drawn in the all-day row, which has no pointer handlers, so the time-grid move never sees them. Not pinned: nothing about them changed.
- The package README and the docs page already say a vertical drag "shifts both" start and end "by the time delta"; that is now true for an event that crosses midnight, so no doc change.
- The brief asked for the suite under `TZ=UTC`, `TZ=America/Los_Angeles` and `TZ=Asia/Shanghai`. Run: all three give `Test Files 56 passed (56)`, `Tests 375 passed | 91 skipped (466)`. That is not three zones measured: the root vitest config sets `UTC` whatever `TZ` is (its pin is `vitest-timezone-pin-8366`), and the new suite-zone cases, which place a `22:00Z` event on the 22:00 row, would fail in any other zone. So the zones are measured through the forks driver, as the calendar's other zone pins are.

## Out of scope: the resize handles have the same piece defect

class (a). Measured once with a one-off jsdom probe at `5ce5efca2` (not committed), week view, a 22:00 Jan 12 to 02:00 Jan 13 event:
- top handle of its first piece dragged to 21:00: `onEventDrop` got `2026-01-12T21:00Z` to `2026-01-13T00:00Z`. The 2 hours after midnight are gone; the README says the end "is preserved".
- bottom handle of its second piece dragged to 03:00: `onEventDrop` got `2026-01-13T00:00Z` to `2026-01-13T03:00Z`. The start moved to midnight.

reach: public door, the week view's resize hands `onEventDrop` a truncated event and `ObjectCalendar`'s default drop handler writes what it is handed. Not fixed here; reported for the seat to file. Dedupe words: week view resize overnight event truncated · time grid resize-top anchorEndMin clipped piece · calendar resize handle loses end past midnight.
